subject: Prepay term structure: split-invoice proposal & ramp schedule (2-3yr)
messages:
From: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@atlas-analytics.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@atlas-analytics.com
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood prepay options — clarifying ramp and invoicing approach

Diego,

Thank you again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to follow up with a concrete ask: Atlas is comfortable with a 2–3 year prepay commitment but we need a pay-structure that matches our budget cycles. Specifically: 

- Can Redwood split the annual prepay into quarterly invoices (so we can align with our quarter budgets) while keeping the committed discount?
- We expect seat usage to ramp: Year 1 = baseline 250k units, Year 2 = 400k, Year 3 (optional) = 650k. Can the discount tiers be structured to adjust by year while preserving an overall blended guarantee?
- Any early-termination credit mechanics? We have procurement policy that requires a pro-rata credit if usage falls >20% below committed at annual true-up.

I attached our RFP terms (ATLAS_RFP_terms_v2.xlsx) showing required billing cadence. Can you share a proposal that maps Redwood pricing to a split-invoice schedule and year-by-year ramp?

Appreciate it — Alice

--
Alice Gomez
Director, Vendor Strategy
Atlas Analytics
From: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@atlas-analytics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood prepay options — clarifying ramp and invoicing approach

Alice — thanks for the clear asks and the RFP. I ran this by Product and Finance and sketched two practical approaches: 

1) Split-invoice with committed blended discount (preferred):
   - Atlas prepays the committed annual amount, invoiced quarterly (4 equal invoices per year).
   - Redwood applies a blended discount on the committed annual volume. Annual true-up reconciles actual usage vs committed; over-usage billed at on-demand rates, under-usage triggers credit per the termination/true-up clause.

2) Year-tiered commitment (more granular):
   - Commit by year with separate discounts per year (e.g., 18% Y1, 22% Y2, 28% Y3). Invoiced quarterly within each year. If Atlas drops below the year commitment by >20%, pro-rata credit applies during the true-up window.

Finance prefers (1) for simpler accounting and to keep guarantees straightforward, but (2) maps more closely to your ramp profile. Both support quarterly invoicing.

I attached a pricing PDF that shows blended vs year-tiered math and a couple of split-invoice templates (split-invoice-examples.pdf).

Before I draft a formal commercial term sheet, can I loop in Marissa and Karthik to get commercial approvals for a 2-year and optional 3rd-year structure? Also: do you have any constraints on how early-termination credits are documented (credit note vs refund)?

Thanks,
Diego
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood prepay options — clarifying ramp and invoicing approach

Diego — reviewed. High-level guidance:

- Approve option (1) blended discount for the 2-year prepay as primary. It simplifies billing and keeps renewals manageable.
- Approve an optional 3rd-year addendum with a higher discount band that must be exercised no later than 90 days before Y3 start.
- For Atlas-specific ramp, we can define the committed baseline as a rolling annual guarantee with annual true-up. If actual usage is >20% below the annual committed baseline, provide a credit note for the difference (applies to the next invoice cycle or can be issued as a credit balance on Atlas account).
- Discount bands: propose 20% off on a 2-year blended with a minimum annual spend floor of $1.2M in Year 1; Year-over-year escalation for higher tiers in the addendum.

Please annotate the pricing PDF with the final numbers for Y1/Y2 and a selectable Y3 addendum, then send the draft to Atlas. Karthik: flag anything finance needs to weigh in on (deferred revenue recognition, refund vs credit).

Marissa
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Couple operational notes:

- Quarterly split invoices for a prepay are fine; Finance will treat them as deferred revenue with quarterly recognition. For accounting clarity, we should include explicit language that invoices are non-refundable prepayments subject to true-up credit mechanics (credit note preferred vs cash refund).
- Early-termination handling: recommend credit note plus option to convert credit into service credits for on-demand usage to reduce cash movements. If Atlas insists on refund, escalate to Legal — possible only with an admin fee and cap.
- Need to ensure the SOW/contract has a clear definition for "committed units" and the true-up window (30 days after year-end).

I can help craft the specific contract language. Once Diego finalizes the proposal numbers, I’ll run the revenue recognition and confirm the pricing bands are acceptable.

Karthik
Director, Finance Partnerships

Alice — attaching the draft commercial summary and two bill-run examples (blended 2-year vs year-tiered). Key points in this proposal: 

- Primary offer: 2-year blended prepay at 20% discount, invoiced quarterly (4 equal invoices/year). Minimum annual spend Year 1 = $1.2M. Annual true-up window = 30 days after year-end.
- Optional addendum: elect 3rd year up to 28% discount if exercised 90 days before Y3 start; Y3 pricing applied only to additional committed volume above the Year 2 baseline.
- Early-termination: credit note for underutilization >20% at true-up (applied to next invoice or held as account credit). Refunds only by exception and subject to admin fee.
- Ramp schedule example: Y1: 250k units, Y2: 400k units (committed), Y3: optional 650k. Over-usage billed at on-demand list.

Files attached: Redwood_2yr-3yr_pricing_table.pdf, split-invoice-examples.pdf. If this reads OK, I’ll convert to an SOW-ready commercial sheet and route to Legal for the addendum language. Any immediate redlines from procurement?

Best,
Diego

Diego — appreciate the fast turnaround. Procurement reviewed and needs two small changes before we can sign: 

1) Replace the default "credit note" remedy with a clause that explicitly allows a cash refund on request (limited to 30% of the prepayment value and subject to a 2% admin fee).
2) Make the quarterly invoices align to our fiscal quarter boundaries (we’ll provide the FY27 billing calendar); we can accept Redwood’s quarterly splits only if calendar-aligned.

If Redwood can accept those two items, procurement is ready to proceed to signature and will prepare a PO. We prefer the blended 2-year approach.

Copying Ravi (Finance) to confirm the spend floor numerics.

Thanks — Alice
